X1.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Message Test
X1.method: Online survey with two parallel groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing the beacon’s reliability and emergency backup capability for remote outdoor activities (e.g., hiking, camping, climbing). Group B receives a message emphasizing regulatory compliance and safety standards for marine operators (e.g., fishing vessels, yacht clubs, marine tour operators). Both messages highlight the FCC registration requirement and compatibility with existing safety kits. Participants are asked: "Would you purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon for personal use at a price of €300–€500?" (Yes/No).
X1.sample: 200 respondents per group, recruited via outdoor recreation forums and marine industry websites, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.
X1.measure: Purchase intent (Yes) and stated willingness to pay (WTP) as a percentage of the price range.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group B because outdoor recreationists value emergency backup in remote areas.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group A because marine safety professionals prioritize regulatory compliance and are willing to invest in equipment that meets standards.

X1.decision_rule: If Group A’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group B’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T1 is supported. If Group B’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group A’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, both theories remain uncertain.

final.target_customer: Outdoor recreationists (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations and who need a reliable emergency backup in environments where other communication methods are unreliable.
final.value_proposition: A 406 MHz distress beacon that provides a reliable emergency backup in remote areas, backed by ACR’s marine safety reputation and FCC registration, offering peace of mind and safety for outdoor activities.
final.next_action: Run the proposed online survey test with 200 respondents per group, measuring purchase intent and willingness to pay. Use the decision rule to determine whether to proceed with a full consumer launch or maintain the current B2B focus.
final.uncertainty: Demand for a consumer beacon among outdoor recreationists is uncertain; the test is needed to validate willingness to pay and actual purchase intent. The market size and competitive landscape are also unknown.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent below 35% or willingness to pay below €300, the favoured theory would shift to T2 and the recommendation would be to target marine safety professionals instead.
If new evidence shows strong demand from marine safety professionals or regulatory compliance drivers, T2 would become more likely and the recommendation would shift accordingly.

arguments.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Message Test
arguments.method: Online survey with two parallel groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing the beacon’s reliability and emergency backup capability for remote outdoor activities (e.g., hiking, camping, climbing). Group B receives a message emphasizing regulatory compliance and safety standards for marine operators (e.g., fishing vessels, yacht clubs, marine tour operators). Both messages highlight the FCC registration requirement and compatibility with existing safety kits. Participants are asked: "Would you purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon for personal use at a price of €300–€500?" (Yes/No).
arguments.sample: 200 respondents per group, recruited via outdoor recreation forums and marine industry websites, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent (Yes) and stated willingness to pay (WTP) as a percentage of the price range.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group B because outdoor recreationists value emergency backup in remote areas.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group A because marine safety professionals prioritize regulatory compliance and are willing to invest in equipment that meets standards.

arguments.decision_rule: If Group A’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group B’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T1 is supported. If Group B’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group A’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, both theories remain uncertain.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available by late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002.
No internal financial data available; reliance on market, product, and regulatory evidence.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12-week timeframe for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about ACR’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be based on evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer product (e.g., personal distress beacon) targeting outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, or marine enthusiasts.
2) Expand the existing B2B product line (emergency beacons and survival lights) into new markets (e.g., commercial fishing, yacht clubs, or government agencies) without a new consumer proposition.
3) No expansion: maintain current product portfolio and distribution channels, focusing on existing B2B customers.
4) License the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology to third-party manufacturers for integration into consumer safety devices, leveraging ACR’s intellectual property without direct consumer branding.

T1.claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency backup in remote areas where other communication methods are unreliable, and they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing they can be found quickly.
T1.who_benefits: Outdoor recreationists (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: These individuals prioritize safety and survival in high-risk environments; they are willing to purchase a device that can transmit a distress signal to emergency services when standard communication fails.
T1.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling the beacons directly to consumers through retail channels or online, leveraging its existing distribution network and brand reputation in marine safety.
assumptions: Outdoor recreationists are aware of the FCC registration requirement for 406 MHz beacons and understand their functionality.
They are willing to pay a premium for a reliable emergency device that integrates with existing safety gear.
Retail or online distribution channels are accessible to this consumer segment.
predictions: Surveyed outdoor recreationists will indicate intent to purchase a 406 MHz beacon at a price point above standard survival lights.
Sales of ACR’s existing marine safety products will not be negatively affected by the new consumer proposition.
A test offering the beacon at outdoor recreation events will generate a higher conversion rate than a generic survival product.
T1.first_claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency backup in remote areas where other communication methods are unreliable, and they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing they can be found quickly.

T2.why_behaviour_changes: Regulatory compliance is a primary driver; these operators must meet safety standards and are willing to invest in equipment that meets those standards, even if it is more expensive than alternative solutions.

B2B distribution channels exist for marine safety products and can reach these operators.

X1.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Message Test
X1.method: Online survey with two parallel groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing the beacon’s reliability and emergency backup capability for remote outdoor activities (e.g., hiking, camping, climbing). Group B receives a message emphasizing regulatory compliance and safety standards for marine operators (e.g., fishing vessels, yacht clubs, marine tour operators). Both messages highlight the FCC registration requirement and compatibility with existing safety kits. Participants are asked: "Would you purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon for personal use at a price of €300–€500?" (Yes/No).
X1.sample: 200 respondents per group, recruited via outdoor recreation forums and marine industry websites, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.
X1.measure: Purchase intent (Yes) and stated willingness to pay (WTP) as a percentage of the price range.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group B because outdoor recreationists value emergency backup in remote areas.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group A because marine safety professionals prioritize regulatory compliance and are willing to invest in equipment that meets standards.

X1.decision_rule: If Group A’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group B’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T1 is supported. If Group B’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group A’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, both theories remain uncertain.

final.value_proposition: A 406 MHz distress beacon that provides a reliable emergency backup in remote areas, backed by ACR’s marine safety reputation and FCC registration, offering peace of mind and safety for outdoor activities.
final.next_action: Run the proposed online survey test with 200 respondents per group, measuring purchase intent and willingness to pay. Use the decision rule to determine whether to proceed with a full consumer launch or maintain the current B2B focus.
final.uncertainty: Demand for a consumer beacon among outdoor recreationists is uncertain; the test is needed to validate willingness to pay and actual purchase intent. The market size and competitive landscape are also unknown.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent below 35% or willingness to pay below €300, the favoured theory would shift to T2 and the recommendation would be to target marine safety professionals instead.

arguments.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Message Test
arguments.method: Online survey with two parallel groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing the beacon’s reliability and emergency backup capability for remote outdoor activities (e.g., hiking, camping, climbing). Group B receives a message emphasizing regulatory compliance and safety standards for marine operators (e.g., fishing vessels, yacht clubs, marine tour operators). Both messages highlight the FCC registration requirement and compatibility with existing safety kits. Participants are asked: "Would you purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon for personal use at a price of €300–€500?" (Yes/No).
arguments.sample: 200 respondents per group, recruited via outdoor recreation forums and marine industry websites, balanced for age, gender, and geographic region.
arguments.measure: Purchase intent (Yes) and stated willingness to pay (WTP) as a percentage of the price range.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group B because outdoor recreationists value emergency backup in remote areas.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and higher WTP than Group A because marine safety professionals prioritize regulatory compliance and are willing to invest in equipment that meets standards.

arguments.decision_rule: If Group A’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group B’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T1 is supported. If Group B’s purchase intent ≥ 45% AND Group A’s purchase intent ≤ 35%, then T2 is supported. If neither condition is met, both theories remain uncertain.

arguments.target_customer: Outdoor recreationists (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations and who need a reliable emergency backup in environments where other communication methods are unreliable.
arguments.value_proposition: A 406 MHz distress beacon that provides a reliable emergency backup in remote areas, backed by ACR’s marine safety reputation and FCC registration, offering peace of mind and safety for outdoor activities.
arguments.next_action: Run the proposed online survey test with 200 respondents per group, measuring purchase intent and willingness to pay. Use the decision rule to determine whether to proceed with a full consumer launch or maintain the current B2B focus.
arguments.uncertainty: Demand for a consumer beacon among outdoor recreationists is uncertain; the test is needed to validate willingness to pay and actual purchase intent. The market size and competitive landscape are also unknown.
would_change_if: If the test shows purchase intent below 35% or willingness to pay below €300, the favoured theory would shift to T2 and the recommendation would be to target marine safety professionals instead.

position.recommendation: Develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting outdoor recreation enthusiasts (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations. Use the existing 406 MHz distress beacon technology and leverage ACR’s brand reputation in marine safety to capture value through direct-to-consumer sales and retail distribution. The evidence base is limited to public sources published

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available by late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002.
No internal financial data available; reliance on market, product, and regulatory evidence.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12-week timeframe for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about ACR’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be based on evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer product (e.g., personal distress beacon) targeting outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, or marine enthusiasts.
2) Expand the existing B2B product line (emergency beacons and survival lights) into new markets (e.g., commercial fishing, yacht clubs, or government agencies) without a new consumer proposition.
3) No expansion: maintain current product portfolio and distribution channels, focusing on existing B2B customers.
4) License the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology to third-party manufacturers for integration into consumer safety devices, leveraging ACR’s intellectual property without direct consumer branding.

T1.claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency backup in remote areas where other communication methods are unreliable, and they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing they can be found quickly.
T1.who_benefits: Outdoor recreationists (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations.
T1.why_behaviour_changes: These individuals prioritize safety and survival in high-risk environments; they are willing to purchase a device that can transmit a distress signal to emergency services when standard communication fails.
T1.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling the beacons directly to consumers through retail channels or online, leveraging its existing distribution network and brand reputation in marine safety.
assumptions: Outdoor recreationists are aware of the FCC registration requirement for 406 MHz beacons and understand their functionality.
They are willing to pay a premium for a reliable emergency device that integrates with existing safety gear.
Retail or online distribution channels are accessible to this consumer segment.
predictions: Surveyed outdoor recreationists will indicate intent to purchase a 406 MHz beacon at a price point above standard survival lights.
Sales of ACR’s existing marine safety products will not be negatively affected by the new consumer proposition.
A test offering the beacon at outdoor recreation events will generate a higher conversion rate than a generic survival product.
T1.first_claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency backup in remote areas where other communication methods are unreliable, and they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing they can be found quickly.

T2.claim: Marine safety professionals and commercial operators will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they are required by regulatory standards and need a reliable backup for emergency situations at sea, leading to higher adoption than outdoor recreationists.

T2.why_behaviour_changes: Regulatory compliance is a primary driver; these operators must meet safety standards and are willing to invest in equipment that meets those standards, even if it is more expensive than alternative solutions.
T2.how_value_is_captured: ACR can capture value by selling beacons through B2B channels (distributors, marine equipment retailers) and by offering bundled safety packages that include beacons and other marine safety products, leveraging its existing marine safety
assumptions: Marine safety professionals are aware of the FCC registration requirement and the need for a 406 MHz beacon.
They prioritize regulatory compliance over price sensitivity when selecting safety equipment.
B2B distribution channels exist for marine safety products and can reach these operators.
The beacon’s reliability and performance are sufficient to meet regulatory standards.
predictions: Surveyed marine safety professionals will indicate intent to purchase a 406 MHz beacon at a price point above consumer survival lights.

X1.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Messaging Test
X1.method: Online survey with two randomized groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing outdoor recreation safety (peace of mind, remote survival, FCC registration requirement). Group B receives a message emphasizing marine safety compliance (regulatory requirement, safety for commercial operators, compliance with international standards). Both messages include a link to a landing page offering a discounted 406 MHz beacon at a price point comparable to standard survival lights (e.g
X1.sample: 500 respondents per group, recruited via outdoor recreation forums, marine industry newsletters, and general consumer panels. Screening to ensure at least 100 respondents per group report participation in relevant activities (hiking, camping, boating, fishing).
X1.measure: Conversion rate (percentage who click the "Learn More" button leading to a product page) and stated intent to purchase ("Would you buy this beacon for yourself or your organization?" Yes/No).

final.target_customer: Outdoor recreationists who participate in activities in remote or wilderness locations and value safety and peace of mind.
final.value_proposition: A reliable, FCC-compliant 406 MHz distress beacon that provides emergency backup for remote activities, marketed as a safety essential for outdoor adventurers, leveraging ACR’s marine safety reputation to build trust and price premium.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Messaging Test (online survey with two randomized groups) to validate demand and willingness to purchase among outdoor recreationists versus marine safety professionals.
final.uncertainty: The size of the outdoor recreation market and its willingness to pay for a 406 MHz beacon are uncertain. There is no direct evidence of consumer demand or price sensitivity. The test will resolve this.
would_change_if: If the test shows Group B (marine safety messaging) achieving higher conversion and intent to purchase, indicating marine safety professionals are the primary drivers of demand, the recommendation would shift toward a B2B-focused expansion.
If neither group shows sufficient conversion or intent, the proposition would be abandoned.

X1.name: Outdoor Recreation vs Marine Safety Message Test
X1.method: Online survey with two parallel randomized message groups. Group A receives a message emphasizing outdoor recreation benefits (peace of mind, safety in remote areas, survival). Group B receives a message emphasizing marine safety benefits (regulatory compliance, safety for commercial vessels, survival at sea). Each participant is asked: "Would you purchase a 406 MHz distress beacon at a price of €250?" (Yes/No). Also ask: "What is the primary reason you would buy?" (Open-ended).
X1.sample: 500 respondents recruited via outdoor recreation forums, marine safety forums, and general consumer panels, balanced for age and gender. Targeting 250 per group.
X1.measure: Conversion rate (Yes answers) and primary reason chosen (coded as outdoor vs marine).

prediction_by_theory.T1: Group A will show higher conversion rate (>=15% more Yes answers) and more responses citing outdoor benefits.
prediction_by_theory.T2: Group B will show higher conversion rate (>=15% more Yes answers) and more responses citing marine benefits.

X1.decision_rule: If Group A conversion >= Group B conversion + 15%, conclude T1 is more likely. If Group B conversion >= Group A conversion + 15%, conclude T2 is more likely. If difference < 15%, both theories remain uncertain.

frame.objective: Determine whether there is sufficient evidence from public sources available by late 2002 to justify ACR Electronics investing in a differentiated consumer proposition built on its 406 MHz satellite distress-beacon technology.
constraints: Limited to public sources published on or before late 2002.
No internal financial data available; reliance on market, product, and regulatory evidence.
Test budget of €20,000 and 12-week timeframe for any proposed experiment.
Uncertainty about ACR’s current reach to individual buyers; must be discovered.
Investment decision must be based on evidence of consumer demand, willingness to pay, and competitive positioning.
alternatives: 1) Develop a differentiated consumer product (e.g., personal distress beacon) targeting outdoor recreation, emergency preparedness, or marine enthusiasts.
2) Expand the existing B2B product line (emergency beacons and survival lights) into new markets (e.g., commercial fishing, yacht clubs, or government agencies) without a new consumer proposition.
3) No expansion: maintain current product portfolio and distribution channels, focusing on existing B2B customers.
4) License the 406 MHz distress-beacon technology to third-party manufacturers for integration into consumer safety devices, leveraging ACR’s intellectual property without direct consumer branding.

T1.claim: Outdoor recreation enthusiasts will adopt 406 MHz distress beacons because they provide a reliable emergency backup in remote areas where other communication methods are unreliable, and they value the peace of mind that comes from knowing they can be found quickly.
T1.who_benefits: Outdoor recreationists (hikers, campers, climbers, boaters) who engage in activities in remote or wilderness locations.

4) Partner with or license tractor technology to third-party manufacturers for consumer applications, leveraging Deere’s engineering without direct consumer branding.
